text: This is Priya. She runs a small pharmacy in Jaipur. Five days ago, she'd never heard of Accel Saathi. Today, her whole shop runs on Accel. And she never made a single phone call.
Last Saturday, UPI failed at rush hour, and she lost customers to the shop next door. So she opened Accel Saathi, and told it what was wrong, in one line.
It found her shop on the GST registry, and asked before using it. Two quick taps, and it knows her business.
Then it turned her problems into a plan. Billing that won't drop. Cameras, for the theft. And backup internet, for when the line goes down.
And it shows its reasoning: what she said, what the catalogue allows, and what real Accel customers actually bought. Every rupee comes from the price list, never from the AI.
Then she says what every owner says: it's too expensive. A desperate salesperson would argue. Saathi gives her choices, each with a price.
She asks which one it recommends. It answers with her own words, and asks for the order.
One clear monthly price. Then KYC: her consent, DigiLocker, and an Aadhaar OTP. About two minutes. No paper. No office.
And when a document is wrong, it says so, in plain words.
She picks her own installation slot, and every service gets a date.
Every step reaches her on WhatsApp. Want an update? She types STATUS. No call centre.
All of this works in ten Indian languages, typed or spoken.
It handles chains too. Five restaurants, each outlet set up for its size, all on one bill, and every outlet tracked to go-live.
And when an owner wants a person, a local partner who speaks her language takes over, and the sale stays theirs.
Every quarter, Accel spends thirty-five lakh rupees on small-business leads it never wins. One in three walks away because of the journey: the visits, the paperwork, the waiting.
Saathi fixes the journey. Live in a week, not eighteen days. If half of them stay, the same leads bring twice the customers, at half the cost each.
Accel Saathi. Every small business, online in one conversation. From Team TouristGuide, NIT Jamshedpur.
